q24005.en: Before moving off again, the driver of a truck must pay special attention to a pedestrian or cyclist who may be in the area just in front of the stopped vehicle.

explain.short: From the high cab the driver cannot see the area just in front of the truck. A pedestrian or cyclist could be hidden there.
explain.rule: A truck driver cannot see the zone just in front of and beside the truck (blind spot). Before moving off he must expect hidden pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.trap: 'zona immediatamente antistante' means the zone right in front: exactly the zone the driver cannot see.

sceneParams.caption: Look out for hidden people before moving off
lines: Truck stopped, about to move off
The zone right in front is hidden

q24006.en: The driver of a truck stopped at a traffic light must expect pedestrians and cyclists that he cannot see because of the shape of his own vehicle.

explain.short: The big body of the truck hides people standing close to it. The driver must imagine they may be there.
explain.rule: A truck driver cannot see the zone just in front of and beside the truck (blind spot). Before moving off he must expect hidden pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.trap: 'prevedere' (expect) is right: you must think of people you cannot see.

sceneParams.caption: Expect people hidden by the truck
lines: Truck waiting at a traffic light
Its body hides people close by

q24007.en: The limited view through a truck's windscreen of the area just in front of the vehicle makes it dangerous for these vehicles to stop in a queue when pedestrians or two-wheelers are around.

explain.short: In a queue, people on foot or on two wheels often pass close to the front of trucks. The driver cannot see them there, so the situation is risky.
explain.rule: A truck driver cannot see the zone just in front of and beside the truck (blind spot). Before moving off he must expect hidden pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.trap: 'limitata visuale' (limited view) is the key: the windscreen does not show the zone right in front.

sceneParams.caption: Queue + people near the front = danger
lines: The windscreen hides the front zone
Bikes and pedestrians may be there

q24008.en: The field of view of trucks allows safe control of the whole area just in front of and beside the vehicle.

explain.short: A truck has big blind spots right in front and at the sides. The driver cannot check all of that area.
explain.rule: A truck driver cannot see the zone just in front of and beside the truck (blind spot). Before moving off he must expect hidden pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.trap: 'tutta la zona' (the whole zone) is wrong: part of it is always hidden.

sceneParams.caption: A truck cannot see the whole front and side zone
lines: Zone in front and at sides is hidden
No full view: blind spots exist

keywords.en: in front and at the side

q24009.en: A pedestrian can cross the road in complete safety by walking very close to the front of a truck stopped in a queue that is about to move off, because the driver can surely see him.

explain.short: Right in front of a truck is exactly where the driver cannot see. Walking there when the truck moves off is very dangerous.
explain.rule: A truck driver cannot see the zone just in front of and beside the truck (blind spot). Before moving off he must expect hidden pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.trap: 'sicuramente avvistabile' (surely visible) is wrong: close to the front, the pedestrian is hidden.

sceneParams.caption: Never walk close to the front of a truck
lines: Truck in a queue, about to move off
The driver cannot see him: danger

q24010.en: When they are about to move off after stopping at a traffic light, truck drivers can easily see pedestrians or cyclists that are beside and brushing against the front of their vehicles.

explain.short: People very close to the front and sides of a truck are in its blind spot. The driver can NOT easily see them.
explain.rule: A truck driver cannot see the zone just in front of and beside the truck (blind spot). Before moving off he must expect hidden pedestrians and cyclists.
explain.trap: 'possono facilmente avvistare' (can easily see) is wrong: these people are hidden.

sceneParams.caption: Truck drivers do NOT easily see people close in front
lines: Truck moves off at a green light
Cyclist right next to its front
Hidden in the blind spot: not seen

q24011.en: The high-visibility retroreflective vest or braces can, in every case, replace the portable warning triangle.

explain.short: The vest makes YOU visible when you walk on the road. The triangle warns drivers about the stopped vehicle. You need both; one does not replace the other.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case) is wrong: the vest never replaces the triangle.

sceneParams.caption: Vest and triangle: you need both

q24012.en: The high-visibility retroreflective vest or braces can only be yellow.

explain.short: High-visibility vests and braces are not only yellow. Fluorescent orange or red ones are also allowed.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is wrong: other bright colours are allowed too.

sceneParams.caption: Not only yellow: orange or red also OK
lines: Yellow, orange or red are allowed

q24013.en: The high-visibility retroreflective vest also protects the driver from chemical risks, heat, fire and electricity.

explain.short: The vest only helps other drivers to see you. It is not protective clothing against chemicals, heat, fire or electricity.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: 'anche' (also) adds protections the vest does not give.

sceneParams.caption: The vest only makes you visible
lines: Vest: makes you easy to see
No protection from fire or heat
No protection from chemicals or power

q24014.en: Inside the vehicle you must keep high-visibility retroreflective vests or braces, as many as the number of seats.

explain.short: The rule is for the driver who gets out on the road. You do not need one vest for every seat.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: 'in numero pari a quello dei posti' (as many as the seats) is wrong: the law does not ask for that.

sceneParams.caption: No need for one vest per seat
lines: Driver gets out on the road
The driver must wear the vest
Not one vest for every seat

q24015.en: You must wear the high-visibility vest when you stop outside built-up areas, while the retroreflective braces must be worn in urban areas.

explain.short: Vest and braces are two equal options for the same rule. Both are for outside towns; braces are not a rule for urban areas.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: The trap splits vest and braces by place ('aree urbane'): in fact they are alternatives for the same case.

sceneParams.caption: Vest OR braces: same rule, outside towns
lines: Vest or braces: you choose one
No special braces rule in towns

q24016.en: The high-visibility retroreflective vest is used to ask passing drivers for help.

explain.short: The vest is not a signal for help. It makes you visible so that passing drivers do not hit you.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: 'serve per chiedere aiuto' (is for asking help) is wrong: its job is safety, being seen.

sceneParams.caption: The vest is for being seen, not for help
lines: It is not a help signal

q24017.en: The high-visibility retroreflective vest is useful only when you have to change a punctured tyre.

explain.short: You need the vest every time you get out of the vehicle on the road outside towns: a breakdown, an accident, placing the triangle, not only for a flat tyre.
explain.rule: Outside towns, when you get out of a stopped vehicle on the road or emergency lane, you wear a high-visibility vest or braces so other drivers see you.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is wrong: the tyre is just one example.

sceneParams.caption: Not only for a flat tyre
lines: Always wear the vest on the road

q24018.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load in danger of falling, it is wise to increase the safe distance, especially uphill.

explain.short: If the load falls, you need space to stop. Uphill, things slide off the back more easily, so keep even more distance.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'specie se si è in salita' (especially uphill) is right: uphill the load falls backwards, towards you.

sceneParams.caption: Load may fall: keep more distance
lines: Truck ahead with a loose load

q24019.en: When driving behind a vehicle with an unstable load, it is wise to increase the safe distance and to overtake it as soon as possible.

explain.short: Stay back to have time to react, and get past the danger as soon as you can do it safely.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'appena possibile' (as soon as possible) means when it is safe and allowed, not at any cost.

sceneParams.caption: Stay back, then overtake when safe
lines: Overtake as soon as it is safe

q24020.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is wise to warn the driver of the possible danger.

explain.short: The driver in front may not know the load is moving. Warning him (for example with a flash of the lights) can prevent an accident.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'avvertire il conducente' (warn the driver) is a good, helpful action here.

sceneParams.caption: Warn the driver about the falling load
lines: Warn him, e.g. flash the lights

q24021.en: When driving behind a vehicle with an unsafe load, it is better not to stay too close, so that you can stop in time if the goods fall.

explain.short: A larger gap gives you the time and space to stop before hitting fallen goods.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'non stargli troppo vicino' (not too close) matches the rule of a longer safe distance.

sceneParams.caption: Not too close: room to stop
lines: You can stop in time if it falls

q24022.en: When driving behind a vehicle with an unstable load, you must be careful, above all when it brakes or turns, because the goods may fall.

explain.short: When a vehicle brakes or turns, its load moves. That is when an unstable load is most likely to fall.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'soprattutto quando frena o svolta' (above all when it brakes or turns) is right: these moves shake the load.

sceneParams.caption: Braking and turning can drop the load
lines: It brakes or turns: load moves

q24023.en: When driving behind a vehicle with a load sticking out, it may be hard to notice that it wants to turn, if the direction indicators are hidden by the hanging goods.

explain.short: Goods hanging off the back can cover the indicators. Then you may not see that the vehicle is about to turn.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'può risultare difficile' (may be hard) is right: hidden indicators give no warning.

sceneParams.caption: Hanging load can hide the indicators
lines: A turn can come without warning

q24024.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is better to keep as close as possible to the left edge of the carriageway.

explain.short: Moving to the left edge puts you in the way of oncoming traffic and does not protect you. The right move is to keep a longer distance.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'margine sinistro' (left edge) is the wrong answer: distance, not position, protects you.

sceneParams.caption: Do not move to the left edge: keep distance

q24025.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying an unsafe load, it is better to move along the left edge of the carriageway.

explain.short: On the left you meet oncoming traffic. You must keep right and simply stay further back.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'margine sinistro' (left edge) is wrong: you stay right and keep distance.

sceneParams.caption: Keep right and stay back
lines: Do not drive along the left edge
Stay right, keep a longer distance

q24026.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is better to overtake it at once, even on a bend.

explain.short: Overtaking on a bend is dangerous because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Overtake only when it is safe.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'anche se in curva' (even on a bend) makes it wrong: never overtake where you cannot see.

sceneParams.caption: Never overtake on a bend

q24027.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying a load that is about to fall, it is better to stop suddenly and move off again only when the other vehicles have passed us.

explain.short: A sudden stop can make the cars behind you crash into you. Just keep a longer distance.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'arrestarsi bruscamente' (stop suddenly) is the danger: it causes rear-end crashes.

sceneParams.caption: No sudden stop: keep distance
lines: Sudden stop: cars behind hit you

q24028.en: When driving behind a vehicle carrying an unstable load, you must reduce the safe distance, so that other vehicles give up overtaking because there is not enough space.

explain.short: With an unstable load ahead you must INCREASE the distance, not reduce it. Blocking other drivers is not your job.
explain.rule: Behind an unstable or falling load: keep a longer safe distance, be ready to stop, warn the driver, and overtake only when it is safe.
explain.trap: 'diminuire' (reduce) is the opposite of the rule.

sceneParams.caption: Increase, never reduce, the distance

q24029.en: Towing a trailer on roads with steep climbs makes the engine coolant temperature rise.

explain.short: Pulling extra weight uphill makes the engine work harder, so it gets hotter. Keep an eye on the temperature.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'fa aumentare la temperatura' (makes the temperature rise) is correct: more effort, more heat.

sceneParams.caption: Trailer + climb = hotter engine

q24030.en: If you tow a trailer, the braking distance increases.

explain.short: The trailer adds weight, so the car needs more road to stop. Keep a longer safe distance.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'aumenta' (increases) is right: more mass, longer stop.

sceneParams.caption: Trailer = longer braking distance

q24031.en: When towing a light trailer, you must consider that the overturning force of the wind is greater.

explain.short: A light trailer is easy for side wind to push and even tip over. Drive slower when it is windy.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'leggero' (light) is the key: less weight, more effect of the wind.

sceneParams.caption: Light trailer: wind pushes it more
lines: Light trailer can tip: slow down

q24032.en: For greater safety, it is advisable to arrange the load in the trailer so that heavy objects are as close as possible to its axle.

explain.short: Heavy things over the trailer's axle keep it balanced and stable. Not at the front, not at the back.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'il più vicino possibile al suo asse' (as close as possible to its axle) is the correct way to load.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy items over the trailer's axle

q24033.en: When driving a vehicle with a trailer, on a right turn you must take special care not to drive the rear wheel onto the pavement.

explain.short: In a turn the trailer's wheels follow a tighter line than the car. On a right turn they can cut the corner and climb the pavement.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'ruota posteriore' (rear wheel) is right: the back wheels cut inside the curve.

sceneParams.caption: Right turn: trailer wheels cut the corner
lines: Trailer wheels take a tighter line
Turn wider: keep off the pavement

q24034.en: When a broken-down vehicle with power steering is towed, turning the steering wheel may be hard work.

explain.short: Power steering works with the engine running. If the broken car's engine is off, the steering wheel is much heavier.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'faticoso' (hard work) is right; heavy, but it still turns.

sceneParams.caption: Towed car: power steering off = heavy wheel

q24035.en: Before towing a trailer, you should make sure that the lighting and signalling systems work properly.

explain.short: The trailer's lights show your braking and turning to drivers behind. Check them all before you leave.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'è opportuno accertarsi' (you should make sure) is right: a quick check before every trip.

sceneParams.caption: Check the trailer's lights first

keywords.it: impianti di illuminazione e di segnalazione

q24036.en: Before starting to tow a trailer, you must check in the rear-view mirrors that visibility is adequate.

explain.short: A trailer can block your view behind. Adjust and check the mirrors (or add extra mirrors) before you set off.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'visibilità sia adeguata' (visibility is adequate) is right: you must see behind the trailer.

sceneParams.caption: Check you can see behind the trailer
lines: Trailer may block the rear view

q24037.en: When trailers are unhitched from the towing vehicle, they must have insurance cover that is valid also for the static risk (when standing still).

explain.short: A trailer parked on its own can still cause damage, for example if it rolls away. So it needs its own insurance also when it stands still.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'rischio statico (da fermo)' (static risk, standing still) is the key: insurance covers it too.

sceneParams.caption: Unhitched trailer: insured even when still
lines: Insurance must cover it standing still

q24038.en: Trailers towed by cars usually have an inertia brake.

explain.short: An inertia brake (freno ad inerzia) works by itself: when the car slows, the trailer pushes on the hitch and its brakes come on.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'in genere' (usually) is right: most car trailers have it, but very light ones may not.

sceneParams.caption: Car trailers usually have an inertia brake

q24039.en: Trailers must have their own number plate.

explain.short: A trailer is a vehicle on its own and is registered, so it carries its own plate.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'targa propria' (own plate) is right: it is not the car's plate.

sceneParams.caption: A trailer has its own plate
lines: A trailer is a vehicle too
It has its own number plate

q24040.en: For more safety when driving a vehicle with a trailer, it is advisable to concentrate the maximum load at the tow hook.

explain.short: Too much weight on the hook overloads the car's rear and makes steering and braking worse. Put heavy items over the trailer's axle.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'in corrispondenza del gancio di traino' (at the tow hook) is the wrong place.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy load over the axle, not on the hook
lines: Max load on the tow hook? No
Put heavy items over the axle

q24041.en: To tow a trailer, you do not need to make the electrical connection between the towing vehicle and the trailer.

explain.short: The electrical connection powers the trailer's lights: brake lights, indicators, rear lights. It is always needed.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'non occorre' (is not needed) is wrong: without it the trailer has no lights.

sceneParams.caption: Electrical connection is always needed
lines: Plug the trailer into the car

q24042.en: To drive a car that tows a broken-down vehicle with a driver on board, you need a Category E driving licence.

explain.short: Towing a broken-down vehicle is an emergency, not driving with a trailer. A normal Category B licence is enough.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'categoria E' is wrong: E is for real trailers, not for towing a broken car.

sceneParams.caption: Towing a broken car: Category B is enough
lines: Not a trailer: B licence is enough

q24043.en: The driver on board a broken-down vehicle that is being towed may have no driving licence.

explain.short: The person in the towed car still steers and brakes it, so they must hold a driving licence.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'può essere privo di patente' (may have no licence) is wrong: a licence is required.

sceneParams.caption: The towed car's driver needs a licence

q24044.en: If a broken-down vehicle is towed with all four wheels on the ground, you must put the gearbox in fourth gear.

explain.short: A towed car must have the gearbox in neutral, so the wheels turn freely. A gear engaged would drag the engine.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'quarta marcia' (fourth gear) is wrong: the correct position is neutral (folle).

sceneParams.caption: Towed car: gearbox in neutral
lines: Broken car towed on four wheels

q24045.en: A vehicle's towing parts do not need to be lubricated regularly.

explain.short: The hook and towing parts move and wear. They must be greased regularly to work well and safely.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'non devono' (must not / need not) is wrong: regular greasing is needed.

sceneParams.caption: Tow parts need regular greasing

q24046.en: A vehicle's towing parts may be non-approved, as long as the trailers towed weigh less than 750 kilograms.

explain.short: The tow hook must always be approved (omologato), whatever the weight of the trailer. The 750 kg figure does not change this.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'possono non essere omologati' (may be non-approved) is wrong; '750 chilogrammi' is a distractor.

sceneParams.caption: Tow hook must always be approved

q24047.en: If you tow a broken-down vehicle with power steering, the steering will always be locked.

explain.short: Without the engine, power steering does not help, so the wheel is heavy. But it is not locked: you can still steer.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'sempre bloccato' (always locked) is wrong: it is hard to turn, not locked.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy steering, but not locked

q24048.en: When towing a trailer on steep descents, you do not need to consider the pushing force of the trailer on the towing vehicle.

explain.short: Downhill the trailer pushes the car forward. You must slow down, use a low gear and brake earlier.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'non occorre tener conto' (no need to consider) is wrong: the push is a real danger.

sceneParams.caption: Downhill the trailer pushes the car

q24049.en: To tow a light trailer, you do not need to make the electrical connection.

explain.short: Even a light trailer needs lights and indicators that work. The electrical connection is always needed.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'leggero' (light) changes nothing: 'non occorre' is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Light trailer: still connect the lights

q24050.en: When you tow a broken-down vehicle, the distance between the two vehicles must be at least 3 metres.

explain.short: The rules set a maximum length for the tow link, not a minimum of 3 metres. The link must be short and well visible.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'almeno 3 metri' (at least 3 metres) is wrong: the rule is about a maximum, not a minimum.

sceneParams.caption: No minimum of 3 m between the vehicles
lines: The tow link has a maximum length

q24051.en: When towing a trailer, you must consider that in tight bends the swept width (the space taken) is smaller.

explain.short: With a trailer the space needed in a tight bend is LARGER, because the trailer cuts inside the curve.
explain.rule: A trailer changes how the car brakes, turns and climbs. Load it well, connect its lights, and know the rules for towing a broken-down car.
explain.trap: 'minore' (smaller) is wrong: it is bigger ('maggiore').

sceneParams.caption: Tight bend + trailer = more space needed
lines: Car with trailer in a tight bend
It needs MORE space, not less

q24052.en: The number of people that vehicles may carry is shown on the registration document.

explain.short: The registration document (carta di circolazione) lists the seats, so it tells you how many people you may carry.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'carta di circolazione' is the right document: not the licence, not the insurance.

sceneParams.caption: Seats are written on the carta di circolazione
lines: It shows the number of seats
That is how many people you may carry

q24053.en: The number of seats of a vehicle is shown on the registration document.

explain.short: Each vehicle's registration document (carta di circolazione) states how many seats it has, driver included.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'numero dei posti' (number of seats) is exactly what the document shows.

sceneParams.caption: Seats are written on the carta di circolazione

q24055.en: The maximum number of seats in cars is nine, including the driver's seat.

explain.short: A car (autovettura) can have at most 9 seats, counting the driver. Bigger vehicles for people are buses.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'compreso quello del conducente' (including the driver's) is right: 9 in total.

sceneParams.caption: Car: max 9 seats, driver included

q24056.en: The number of people that cars may carry can be at most nine, including the driver.

explain.short: A car has at most 9 seats, and the driver counts as one of them.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'al massimo di nove, compreso il conducente' (at most nine, driver included) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Car: max 9 people, driver included

q24057.en: The number of people that motorcycles may carry is always two, besides the driver.

explain.short: A motorcycle can carry at most one passenger, and only if the registration document allows it. Never two, and not 'always'.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'sempre di due' (always two) is wrong: the maximum is one passenger.

sceneParams.caption: Motorcycle: at most 1 passenger
lines: Only if the document allows it

q24058.en: The number of people that cars may carry is at most four.

explain.short: Cars can have up to 9 seats, driver included. The real number is on the registration document.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'al massimo di quattro' (at most four) is wrong: the limit is nine.

sceneParams.caption: Cars: up to 9, not 4

q24059.en: The number of people that trucks may carry is always five, including the driver.

explain.short: There is no fixed number for trucks. Each truck's registration document shows its own number of seats.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'sempre di cinque' (always five) is wrong: it depends on the vehicle.

sceneParams.caption: Trucks: seats as on the document

q24060.en: The number of people that a vehicle may carry, shown on the registration document, does not include the driver.

explain.short: The number on the registration document counts all seats, the driver's seat too.
explain.rule: The registration document (carta di circolazione) shows the number of seats, driver included. A car has at most 9 seats.
explain.trap: 'non comprende il conducente' (does not include the driver) is wrong: the driver is included.

sceneParams.caption: The number includes the driver

q24061.en: The panel shown must be placed at the end of the load that sticks out behind the vehicle.

explain.short: The panel marks the very end of the overhanging load, so drivers behind see where it really ends.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'all'estremità del carico' (at the end of the load) is right: not on the vehicle body.

sceneParams.caption: Panel at the end of the overhanging load
lines: Load sticks out at the back
Panel at the very end of the load

q24062.en: The panel shown signals loads that stick out from the rear of the vehicle.

explain.short: This red and white striped panel tells drivers behind that the load sticks out beyond the back of the vehicle.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'parte posteriore' (rear) is right: the panel is for rear overhangs.

sceneParams.caption: It marks a load sticking out at the back
lines: Load sticks out at the rear

q24063.en: The panel shown must be retroreflective.

explain.short: Retroreflective means it shines back in headlights. So drivers see the load at night too.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'retroriflettente' (retroreflective) is right: it must be seen in the dark.

sceneParams.caption: The panel must reflect light

q24064.en: The panel shown is used when the load sticks out behind the vehicle, even by only a little.

explain.short: Any load that sticks out at the back needs the panel, even a short overhang.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'anche se di poco' (even by a little) is right: there is no minimum.

sceneParams.caption: Even a small rear overhang needs the panel
lines: Load sticks out a little at the back

q24065.en: The panel shown can be put on broken-down vehicles when they are towed and the hazard lights do not work.

explain.short: If a towed broken-down vehicle cannot use its hazard lights, this panel can mark its back so drivers behind see it.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'può' (can) is right: it is an allowed option when hazard lights do not work.

sceneParams.caption: Also for a towed car without hazard lights
lines: Broken car towed, no hazard lights
The panel can mark its back

q24066.en: The panel shown must be fixed at the end of the load sticking out from the vehicle, so that it is always clearly visible.

explain.short: The panel only works if drivers behind can see it, so it goes at the end of the load in plain view.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'sempre ben visibile' (always clearly visible) is right: it must not be hidden.

sceneParams.caption: At the load's end, always visible
lines: Panel at the end of the load

q24067.en: The panel shown asks drivers behind the vehicle it is fixed on to drive with special care.

explain.short: The panel warns that a load sticks out at the back. Drivers behind must keep their distance and be careful.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'particolare prudenza' (special care) is right: that is the message of the panel.

sceneParams.caption: Drivers behind: be careful
lines: Load sticks out at the back
Drivers behind: keep distance, be careful

q24068.en: The panel shown is used only if the load sticks out by more than three tenths of the vehicle's length.

explain.short: The panel is needed for ANY rear overhang, even a small one. Three tenths (3/10) is the maximum a load may stick out, not the starting point for the panel.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'solo se ... oltre tre decimi' (only if more than 3/10) is wrong: the panel is needed even for a little.

sceneParams.caption: Panel for any rear overhang, not only over 3/10
lines: Any load sticking out at the back

q24069.en: The panel shown must also be placed on the side, when the load sticks out beyond the vehicle's width.

explain.short: This panel is for loads that stick out at the BACK. It is not a side signal.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'anche di lato' (also on the side) is wrong: the panel is only for the rear.

sceneParams.caption: Rear only, not on the side
lines: Panel: for loads sticking out behind
It is not used on the sides

q24070.en: The panel shown identifies trucks specialised in carrying building materials.

explain.short: The panel is not a label for a type of truck. It marks any load sticking out at the back.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'identifica gli autocarri specializzati' (identifies special trucks) is wrong: it is about the load, not the truck.

sceneParams.caption: It marks an overhanging load, not a truck type
lines: Not a label for a type of truck
It marks a load sticking out behind

q24071.en: The panel shown must be placed on vehicles that carry rubbish.

explain.short: Rubbish trucks do not need this panel just because of what they carry. It is only for loads sticking out at the back.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'spazzatura' (rubbish) has nothing to do with this panel.

sceneParams.caption: Not for rubbish trucks: for rear overhangs
lines: Not linked to the type of goods
Only for loads sticking out behind

q24072.en: The panel shown must be placed on vehicles only if the load sticks out by at least 50 centimetres.

explain.short: There is no minimum: the panel is needed even if the load sticks out only a little. 50 cm is the size of the panel's side, not an overhang limit.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'solo se ... almeno 50 centimetri' (only if at least 50 cm) is wrong: even a little overhang needs it.

sceneParams.caption: No minimum overhang for the panel
lines: Load sticks out even a little

q24073.en: The panel shown must be placed on the back of all trucks.

explain.short: The panel is needed only when a load sticks out at the back, not on every truck.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'tutti gli autocarri' (all trucks) is wrong: only vehicles with an overhanging load.

sceneParams.caption: Not on all trucks: only with rear overhang

q24074.en: The panel shown can be replaced by a red flag measuring 50x50 centimetres.

explain.short: Only this retroreflective striped panel is valid. A red flag cannot replace it.
explain.rule: The red-white striped panel marks a load sticking out at the back. It is retroreflective and goes at the end of the load.
explain.trap: 'bandiera di colore rosso' (red flag) is wrong: the 50x50 size belongs to the panel itself.

sceneParams.caption: No red flag: only the striped panel
lines: A red flag is not allowed instead
